provenance_model.principle: Provenance is a FIXED property of each field (by field identity), never a mislabelable per-category flag. Three classes:

derived.rule: value == tools/workload_ceiling.py(tags) EXACTLY (positive equality, both directions). No citation. To raise a value, fix the TAGS not the envelope. Helper is a PURE function of tags only (never reads the envelope) — a test asserts its signature.

framework-judgment.rule: Expert ordinal, NOT reconstructable from any tag. Same epistemic class as the already-unsourced hardware_opportunity(1-4) (the taxonomy header explicitly designates that 'framework content, not account/market claims'). sources=[], no citation, but honestly labelled a judgment — never called 'derived'. The ceiling helper has NO rule for these; the test does NOT recompute a ceiling for them.

sourced.rule: Asserts an external real-world fact. Non-null REQUIRES a real citation in `sources` at confidence A/B (retention) or A/B/C (per_unit). null wherever no category-wide fact exists (never guess).

fields.name: scaling_driver
fields.rule: The ONE metric a category's iron scales with (the SE discovery question). Non-empty wherever hardware_profile is non-empty; null only when hardware_profile==[]. Contains NO digit character (spelled-out magnitudes only, like the existing infrastructure_notes). ~12/58 cats can lift the phrase from an infrastructure_notes 'sized by ...' clause (delete it from prose in the same edit); the other ~38 non-empty-profile cats need a freshly authored phrase.

fields.name: latency_class
fields.fill_note: spot-check: a genuinely latency-sensitive category that is neither edge nor time-series tagged must not be artificially capped at 'interactive' by INV-11 — if the sales story needs 'real-time', add the edge/time-series tag that justifies it rather than under-rating latency.

fields.name: concurrency
fields.meaning: typical simultaneous users/sessions/jobs the category's deployment serves. single=one operator/station; low=small team, single-digit; moderate=department, tens; high=enterprise, hundreds; massive=multi-tenant/thousands (SaaS-operator platform, VDI farm, multi-tenant inference). Orthogonal to facility size beyond the category's intrinsic multi-tenancy, which is exactly why it is a standalone queryable band. NOT constrained by an empty hardware_profile — a SaaS-light category can be 'massive'.

fields.name: retention_horizon
fields.rule: Band ONLY where a category-wide legal/standard retention window genuinely exists (imaging retention statutes, GxP/Part 11 records, HIM chart law) + a confidence A/B citation in sources. Else null. NO coupling to capacity-archive presence (INV-9 dropped — retention is orthogonal to owning an archive tier).

fields.name: per_unit_data_size
fields.rule: The ONLY numeric atom. Non-null => value_low<=value_high AND confidence in {A,B,C} (never D) AND source is a real citation NOT in {structural-inference,TODO,derived,inference,'',n/a} AND source appears in `sources`. Else null.

fields.name: sources
fields.rule: Citations backing the sourced fields (retention_horizon, per_unit_data_size). [] when both are null. Nothing else consumes it.

fields.name: notes
fields.rule: Non-sizing prose only. Contains NO digit character.

STEP6 SaaS-light (hardware_profile==[]): degenerate template (gpu_role none, storage bands none, data_growth static/low, availability best-effort/standard, per_unit null; concurrency assigned honestly, may be massive).
